waveName: Wave 5 – Undo/redo & stone editing, scale performance, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI

package.title: Per-sheet legends, readable cut templates, complete compact coordinates, readable overview
package.goal: Each laying sheet carries its own colour key and stone counts. Cut-template dimensions never overlap text. The coordinate appendix covers 100 % of stones in a fraction of the pages. The overview of large projects stays readable.
steps:
Per-sheet legend:
- Data from computeStats(range = the sheet, the shared cache).
- Header 'Steine auf diesem Blatt: N, davon K zugeschnitten', then chips of about 45×4.5 mm with swatch, code, material colour number or short name, and ×count.
- Place it in the free band below the joint label, otherwise in a free right column, otherwise on a 'Legende zu Blatt X' page that follows. Never truncate.
- Draw swatches as 'F' plus a separate 'S', never 'FD'. No 'Kontrollstrecke' on continuation pages.

templateLayout.ts: pure layoutTemplate(ci, group, boxW, measure).
- Measure the text first; warnings come first in the text block.
- Choose zoom from [10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1].
- Dimension lines at a fixed 2.5 mm paper offset, with extension lines, labels parallel to the edge and an outward normal from the orientation.
- Collision pass against title, text, the 1:1 contour, other labels and cut lines; leader lines as fallback.
- Wrapped lines advance by lines × 2.4 mm. No dropped lines; the row height follows the content.
drawTemplate only renders the result.

coords.ts: buildCompactCoords(layout, data, palette, sections, opts).
- Column table and row table, with 'Zuschnitt' marks on edge columns and rows.
- Per section, one colour-run line per row, e.g. 'K: 001–006 → 09 · 007 ◆ …'.
- Exception rows for non-FULL pieces, FULL pieces that need a cut, and pieces whose raw size differs from the grid tile.
- A control sum equal to section stats pieces; on mismatch draw an error box.
pdfOptions: coordMode 'compact' | 'perStone' | 'off', default 'compact'. includeCoords=false maps to 'off'. coordLimit applies only to perStone. Update planPdfPages.

Overview map-grid mode: when the median section is under 10 mm on paper, or labels would exceed 70 % of a section, draw thin section lines plus column numbers and row letters along the edges, with a caption, and no per-cell boxes. Otherwise use font-relative label boxes in the corner. Selected sections get a thicker outline and a light fill. Each section cover gets a small locator thumbnail (one embedded image alias).
acceptance: The per-sheet legend counts, summed over a section's sheets, equal secStats.perColor pieces. The existing per-colour fill test stays green and unchanged.

layoutTemplate on 3/5/10/12 mm configurations and one 20 mm-raw material configuration: no label box intersects the title, the text block, the 1:1 contour or another label; each label equals f1(ci.edges[i]); text never exceeds the box.

Compact coordinates: every stone's (X, Y, colour) can be reconstructed from the tables plus the exceptions and equals cellPieces. The 200×100 cm, 5 mm case needs ≤ 70 coordinate pages (today 329 pages covering only 35 %).
A 10000×5000 mm project with 300 mm sections uses map-grid mode.
package.risk: Effort L. The compact coordinate format changes the documented output; keep perStone available. planPdfPages must stay equal to the actual page count.

findings.title: Laying sheets have no legend of their own (code → colour/material, count per sheet)
findings.problem: A laying sheet shows only numeric codes. Mapping '21' to a colour name or material number and knowing how many stones of each colour that sheet needs requires flipping to the section cover or the global legend. Sheets are the pages used at the work table and are often separated from the rest of the document.
findings.evidence: drawSheet (pdf.ts:540-693) draws stones, rulers, crosses, hint and calibration only; the legend exists only per section/project (pdf.ts:515-524, 318-339). Free space exists: out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf p9 mosaic ends at y≈232 mm while the footer starts at ≈281 mm, about 45 mm unused (png/a5-09.png).
findings.proposal: Count pieces per colour while drawing the sheet (the loop already visits every piece). Render a legend strip in the footer: swatch, 2-digit code, colour name (short), material colour number, count on this sheet, as 22×4.5 mm chips wrapping in rows. Size the bottom reserve dynamically: compute the needed legend rows before choosing printH, or continue on a 'Legende zu Blatt A1-1' page if it doesn't fit. Add a per-sheet total ('Steine auf diesem Blatt: 986, davon 41 zugeschnitten'). Counts come from the same pieces drawn, consistent with the PDF=preview test.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts:
(a) For each sheet, compute the counts with the existing core function: const sheetStats = computeStats(layout, data, palette, materials, {reservePct, groutDepthMm}, {r0, r1, c0, c1}, cache). Do not count by hand while drawing. This reuses the same piece and cut logic as the section and global legends, and the sheet totals add up exactly to the section totals (checked: 1059 + 793 = 1852 stones, 142 + 158 = 300 cut).
(b) Size the bottom reserve per section, not globally, before calling tilesOf and choosing s. Use the number of colours the section uses (secStats.perColor with pieces > 0) as an upper bound for any of its sheets: legendRows = ceil(nColorsSection / chipsPerRow), bottomReserve = 21 + 4 + legendRows * 5 mm, then printH = PH - M - topReserve - bottomReserve. Pass printH into tilesOf instead of the closure constant. If legendRows would take more than about 25% of the page height (very large palettes on A4), keep the normal reserve and print a separate 'Legende zu Blatt A1-n' page right after that sheet.
(c) Draw the legend between the mosaic/joining label and the existing hint/calibration line. Make compact chips of about 22 x 4.5 mm: swatch, 2-digit code, the material colour number if one is assigned (otherwise a shortened colour name), and 'xN' for this sheet. Above them, put one line: 'Steine auf diesem Blatt: N, davon K zugeschnitten'. Add the material colour number to the section legend table (pdf.ts:515-524) too.
(d) Keep the PDF==preview test valid. Either draw the swatch fill and its border as separate paths (fill with 'F', border with 'S'), or tag the legend region and make countFills in tests/pdf.test.ts ignore it. Then add a test that the per-sheet legend counts summed over a section's sheets equal secStats.perColor[].pieces, and that the per-sheet totals summed over all sheets equal stats.pieces.

Add a per-sheet legend to drawSheet in src/core/pdf.ts without changing the sheet tiling.

1. Data: at the start of drawSheet, call computeStats(layout, data, palette, materials, {reservePct, groutDepthMm}, {r0,r1,c0,c1}, cache). This is the same function and the same cache used by the section cover (pdf.ts:461-469). Do not hand-count in the draw loop. Use st.perColor.filter(c => c.pieces > 0), sorted by code, plus st.pieces and st.cutPieces. The sum over all sheets equals the section and project totals (verified in 5 configs).

2. Content: a header line "Steine auf diesem Blatt: N, davon K zugeschnitten" (new i18n key pdf.sheetStones with {n},{k}). One chip per colour:
   - swatch, 2-digit code and "×count"
   - the material colour number when palette[i].materialId is set, otherwise a short name truncated with maxWidth
   Use chips about 45 mm wide and 4.5 mm high, wrapping (4 per row on A4 portrait, 8 on A3 landscape).

3. Placement (tilesOf/printH stay unchanged, so the geometry, crosses and sheet numbers are identical to today):
   (a) Put the legend in the free band between py(botE)+7 mm (below the "↓ Anschluss" label at py(botE)+3.4) and PH-M-12 (above sideInfo, markHint and calibration) if it fits. This works for all sheets in small, A3 and fit-to-page projects, and for edge sheets in large ones.
   (b) Otherwise, use the free right-hand column if it is at least 45 mm wide.
   (c) Otherwise, add a continuation page directly after the sheet, titled "Legende zu Blatt A1-3" (new key pdf.sheetLegendFor), using the same chips. Never truncate silently.
   Optionally offer a PDF option for a fixed extra bottom reserve (e.g. +10 mm, a constant independent of content) for users who prefer fewer continuation pages.

4. Swatches: draw the fill with rect(...,'F') and the outline with a separate rect(...,'S'), never 'FD', so the 'B' operator stays reserved for stones on sheet pages. Do not reuse table() on sheet pages. Keep the "Kontrollstrecke" text off continuation pages, so the existing test filter still excludes them.

5. Tests (tests/pdf.test.ts):
   - For each sheet stream, the 'B' fill count per colour must equal that sheet's legend counts. Expose the per-sheet stats via an optional onSheet callback, or recompute them in the test with computeStats over the same ranges.
   - The legend counts summed over all sheets must equal stats.perColor[i].pieces and stats.pieces.
   - The existing PDF==preview assertion must stay unchanged and green.
   - Add the new keys to de/en/tr (tests/i18n.test.ts enforces parity).

findings.title: Cut-template dimension labels print over the title and the info text, so dimensions are hard to read
findings.problem: Edge-length labels are pushed outward by 0.9 raw-mm, and that offset is multiplied by the zoom (pdf.ts:781; zoom is 6 for 5 mm stones, so 5.4 mm on paper). Top-edge labels land in the title row. Bottom-edge labels land on the first info line, which starts at a fixed oy+rawH*zoom+3.5 (pdf.ts:783). Info lines wrap through maxWidth but only advance 2.8 mm per logical line (pdf.ts:795-799), so the 'Farben' list prints over the ID list. There are no dimension lines, so a label can sit on the dashed raw-stone outline and read like a raw-stone size. For cut dimensions this is a misreading risk, which requirement 18 forbids.
findings.evidence: /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/pdf-print/tplcollide.ts (replicates drawTemplate placement): 5 mm stones: 103/103 templates have at least one collision (75 labels in the title band, 63 in the text block). 10 mm: 101/154 (66 %). 12 mm: 42/66 (64 %). Visual png/tplhi-14-row1.png: in T1, the bottom label '2,5' prints over the '5 mm' in 'Außenmaß: 2,5 × 5 mm' and a '2,5' sits next to 'Vorlage T1'. In T2 the '5' sits on the raw-stone border. overlap.py finds 6–16 overlapping word pairs on every template page (e.g. a4p_5mm p15–p25, tr_a4 p12/13). en_a4_3mm p8: wrapped 'Farben' list over the IDs ('11,' x 'I042-1,').
findings.proposal: Rewrite drawTemplate's annotation step. For each polygon edge, draw a real dimension line offset outward by a fixed paper distance (2.5 mm, not multiplied by zoom), with extension lines and arrowheads; put the label parallel to the edge with a white background. Reserve the space: oy = yv + 13, text block start = oy + rawH*zoom + 7. Run a simple box-collision pass (label vs label, title, text, 1:1 contour) and fall back to a leader line to the side. For info lines, use doc.splitTextToSize and advance by lines.length*2.4 mm. Pick zoom as the largest of {1, 1.5, 2, 3, …} that fits the free box (e.g. a 20 mm raw stone gets 1.5:1 instead of 1:1). Values stay exactly ci.edges/ci.angles/ci.cutLines; only placement changes.
corrected:
Rework drawTemplate in src/core/pdf.ts (lines 743-810). Only placement changes: the printed values stay exactly ci.edges, ci.angles, ci.w/h/area and ci.cutLines.

1) Measure the text first. Build the info lines and put warnings early: raw, outer, then nonConvex/notFitting, then angles, cut lines, colours, IDs. Wrap each with doc.splitTextToSize(line, w-3) at 5.5 pt. textH = number of printed lines × 2.4 mm.

2) Choose the scale from the space that is left. Title band: 6.5 mm. Dimension reserve: DIM = 3 mm on each side. contourW = bbox(polyInRaw).maxX + 3 (the 1:1 contour plus a gap) when zoom > 1. Available height = h - 6.5 - 2*DIM - textH - 1. Available width = w - 2*DIM - 2 - contourW. Pick zoom as the largest of [10, 8, 6, 5, 4, 3, 2, 1.5, 1] that fits both. Print the scale with f1(zoom) so 1.5 reads '1,5:1'. Set oy = yv + 6.5 + DIM. If even zoom 1 does not fit, shorten the ID list (it already ends with '…'). Never drop the warnings, the cut lines or the outer size.

3) Dimensions. For every polygon edge, draw a dimension line parallel to the edge, offset outward by a fixed DIM*0.8 mm of paper (do not multiply by zoom). Add thin extension lines from both vertices and small arrow ticks. Put the label at the midpoint, rotated parallel to the edge (doc.text with angle, kept between -90 and 90 degrees), on a white filled rectangle sized with doc.getTextWidth. Edges shorter than 4 mm on paper get a short leader line to a free spot outside the drawing.

4) Collisions. Collect label boxes. Check each one against the title band, the text block (which starts at oy + rawH*zoom + DIM + 1.5), the 1:1 contour box and the labels already placed. On a hit, slide the label along the edge, then use the leader-line fallback. Use one helper that returns these boxes for both drawing and testing.

5) Text loop. For each wrapped line array, call doc.text(arr, x+1.5, ty) and then add arr.length * 2.4 to ty. Remove the silent `break` and assert instead, since step 2 guarantees the text fits.

6) Header. Shorten or shrink the shape name so it does not run into 'Vorlage Tnn'. At the moment 'Individuell zugeschnitten · 5×' prints over 'Vorlage T13' (t10 p18).

7) Test. Export the pure placement helper from step 4 (for example layoutTemplateBox(ci, w, h, measure)). Add a vitest that runs collectTemplates on the portrait, landscape, animal and city samples at 3, 5, 10 and 12 mm stones and asserts that no label, title, text or contour boxes overlap and that no info line is dropped.

Effort: M. Impact: 4.

Only placement in src/core/pdf.ts drawTemplate changes. Every printed number stays exactly f1(ci.edges[i]), ci.angles and ci.cutLines.

1. Pure layout first. Add src/core/templateLayout.ts with layoutTemplate(ci, group, boxW, measure). `measure` wraps doc.getTextWidth and doc.splitTextToSize. The function returns: zoom, drawing origin, dimension lines, label boxes and anchors, text lines with y-positions, and requiredHeight. drawTemplate only renders this result, which makes the layout testable in vitest.

2. Text block measured up front:
   - Build the lines as now, but put the warnings (pdf.nonConvex, pdf.notFitting) FIRST, in red.
   - Wrap each line with splitTextToSize(line, w-3) and advance lines.length × 2.4 mm (5.5 pt × 1.15 ≈ 2.23 mm).
   - Delete the silent `break` (pdf.ts:796). No line may ever be dropped.

3. Zoom and box size:
   - Choose zoom as the largest of [1, 1.5, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 8, 10] such that the drawing plus 2 × 5 mm dimension bands plus the true-size 1:1 contour (only if zoom > 1, plus a 3 mm gap) fits boxW.
   - Height: title band (9 mm) + drawing + bands + measured text must fit; otherwise use the next smaller zoom.
   - Zoom is never below 1. If zoom 1 still does not fit, let the template span two columns.
   - Replace the fixed boxH = 68 with a per-row height: the max requiredHeight of the templates in that row. The page break uses that height.
   - Print the scale as f1(zoom) + ':1'.

4. Dimensioning:
   - For each edge i of ci.polyInRaw, draw a dimension line parallel to the edge at a fixed PAPER offset of 2.5 mm (not × zoom).
   - Use the outward normal from the polygon orientation (sign of the signed area), not the direction from the centroid.
   - Thin extension lines start at the two piece vertices. Add small arrowheads or 45° ticks.
   - Label text: f1(ci.edges[i]). Keep it horizontal for axis-parallel edges. For slanted edges, set it parallel with the angle normalized to (-90°, 90°], so it is never upside-down. Compute the rotated anchor by hand and pass align 'left'.
   - If an edge is under 4 mm on paper, put the label outside with a short leader.
   - Collision pass. Obstacles: other labels, the title row, the text block, the 1:1 contour, the piece contour and the red cut lines. Try offsets 2.5, then 4.5, then 6.5 mm, then a side leader.
   - Any white label background must never cover a cut line or the 1:1 contour.
   - Draw the raw-stone size in grey (or only in the 'Rohstein' text line) so black dimensions always mean the piece.

5. Optional, low cost:
   - Mark each non-90° interior angle at its vertex with a small arc and f1(ci.angles[i], 1)°. Today's angle list has no vertex reference.
   - Add a 50 mm Kontrollstrecke (drawCalibration) to template pages so users can verify the 1:1 print. If you do, tighten the stream filter in tests/pdf.test.ts (currently "s.includes('Blatt') && s.includes('Kontrollstrecke')") so template fills are not counted as laid stones.

6. Tests:
   - Vitest on layoutTemplate for all templates of the 3/5/10/12 mm sample configs, plus a 20 mm-raw material config:
     - no label box intersects another label, the title, the text block or the 1:1 contour;
     - every label string === f1(ci.edges[i]);
     - rendered logical lines === built lines;
     - text bottom <= box bottom.
   - An e2e/pdftotext -bbox check (like pdf-print/overlap.py) asserting 0 overlapping word pairs on template pages.

findings.title: Coordinate pages fill up to 70 % of the PDF yet cover only a fraction of the stones
findings.problem: The coordinate list prints one 4.2 mm row per stone, using fixed 182 mm column widths (pdf.ts:850-856). Most rows repeat information (the X/Y of a whole stone follows from its ID), so the list is long but covers few stones. On A3 or custom paper half the width is empty. The X/Y columns are the piece's bounding-box minimum, which is not stated; for triangles this point is not a corner of the stone.
findings.evidence: out/big_200x100.pdf: 333 of 489 pages are coordinates. out/big_500x250.pdf: 336 of 1134 pages, covering 20 000 of about 155 000 stones (~13 %). out/a4p_5mm_1to1.pdf: 49 coordinate pages for 3655 stones (pages 26-74). A3 landscape coordinate page uses only the left half (png/a3-montage.png). persize.ts: the 200×100 cm project has only 1914 non-standard (cut) pieces.
findings.proposal: Per section, print (1) a compact axis table 'Spalte n → X von–bis' and 'Zeile → Y von–bis' (cols+rows lines, e.g. 51+34 instead of 1852 rows); with the ID this defines every whole stone exactly. (2) Full rows only for cut/subdivided/freeform pieces: ID, code, shape, outer size, bounding-box X/Y min–max, T#. Flow rows in 2–3 columns when PW−2M ≥ 2×tableWidth. Retitle the X/Y headers 'X/Y links oben (Begrenzungsrechteck)'. Rough estimate for 200×100 cm: about 2250 rows (≈35 pages) covering 100 % of stones instead of 333 pages covering 78 %, so coordLimit is mostly unnecessary; keep CSV for the flat list.

findings.title: PDF coordinate lists take 69 % of the pages and 42 % of the time but still cover only about a third of the stones
findings.problem: By default includeCoords is on and coordLimit is 20,000. The PDF then prints one table row per stone (pdf.ts:813 to 864) until the limit is reached, then stops with a 'truncated, use the CSV' notice. For any project over 20k stones the result is hundreds of pages, an incomplete list, and only the first sections covered. Every uncut stone's X and Y are already fully determined by its column and row (colX[col], rowY[row]), so most rows repeat information.
findings.evidence: 200x100 cm, 5 mm tiles, 1 mm joint, A4 1:1, all 28 sections (bench-pdf.ts): 474 pages, 2.7 MB, 4.03 s, of which the coords phase takes 1.68 s; peak RSS 183 MB rising to 471 MB. Page classification with pdftotext: 329 coordinate pages, 98 laying sheets, 28 section covers, 13 template pages, 7 other (pdf/200x100-5mm-a4.pdf). The last page reads 'Die Koordinatenlisten wurden nach 20000 Steinen gekürzt', i.e. 20,000 of 56,783 stones (35 %). coord-compact.ts shows that a complete exact list for this project needs only 4,505 rows: 2,505 per-section column-X and row-Y entries plus 2,000 non-full pieces. Paths are under /tmp/claude-0/-home-user-MosaicPlan/2af1e5b3-d1bd-540e-aeb5-6edf8b6b0ca5/scratchpad/audit/performance-scale/.
findings.proposal: Print exact coordinates compactly. Per section, add a column table (column no., X start, width) and a row table (row label, Y start, height): every rectangular stone's origin is (X_col, Y_row), which is complete and exact. Add per-piece rows only for cells that are not FULL (DIAG, LINE, SUB, FREE: piece ID, bbox X/Y, template T#). For the measured project that is about 4.5k rows, roughly 70 pages instead of 329, covering 100 % of stones instead of 35 %, and the coordLimit truncation can go away. Keep the per-stone CSV for spreadsheet use.

   - Header line: 'Every uncut stone at row R, column C has its top-left corner at (X_C, Y_R) and size width_C × height_R.'

2. Colour recipe per row, required, per section: one line per row, built from runs of identical FULL cells, for example 'C | 1–5: 17 · 6–21: 15 · 22: ◢ (see C022) · 23–40: 13'. A non-FULL cell breaks the run and points to its entry in table 3. This keeps every FULL stone's colour code in the PDF, which matters because pdf.ts:565 hides codes on the sheets when cells are under 2.2 mm on paper. Measured cost: 7 to 12 pages for 30x40 cm with 2 mm tiles, instead of 220.

3. Piece table only for non-FULL cells (DIAG_A/B, LINE, SUB, FREE). Columns as today: ID-i, bbox X/Y, code, shape, size, cut + T#. Build it with the same cellPieces() and pieceCutInfo() calls as today, so cut dimensions come only from the computed geometry.

4. Control sum per section: print 'Σ run lengths + non-FULL pieces = N stones'. Assert in code that N equals secStats.pieces (from computeStats with the section range). If the check fails, print an error box rather than a silently wrong list (requirement 18).

5. Options:
   - In pdfOptions.ts, replace includeCoords/coordLimit with coordMode: 'compact' | 'perStone' | 'off', default 'compact'. coordLimit applies only to 'perStone', and the truncation notice stays only there.
   - In StepPdf.tsx, add a select with a hint giving the estimated page count for each mode.
   - Add i18n keys to de/en/tr.

6. Tests (vitest): for the four sample projects plus one with 2 mm tiles, one with cut-end and one with cut-both edges, rebuild every stone (ID, X/Y, colour) from the compact listing data (export it as a pure function, e.g. buildCompactCoords() in a new src/core/coords.ts that pdf.ts calls). Check it against cellPieces() for every cell: exact match, each stone counted once, total equal to computeStats().pieces. Also check that the PDF page count drops for the 200x100 cm / 5 mm case.

The per-stone CSV stays unchanged. Effort is M rather than S.

findings.title: The overview of a large project becomes a solid block of labels
findings.problem: The overview draws a fixed 5 mm-high orange label box per section (pdf.ts:290-293), while the font is clamped to a minimum of 5 pt (pdf.ts:284). Once a section is about 6 mm or less on paper, the labels cover the whole preview, so the overview no longer shows where a section lies in the picture. Sheet boundaries are never shown.
findings.evidence: png/huge-04-top.png (out/huge_overview.pdf, 10×5 m, 578 sections in 34×17): the mosaic preview is fully hidden behind the orange 'A1…Q34' boxes.
findings.proposal: Make the box height font-relative (fontPt*0.3528*1.35). When a section is under ~10 mm on paper, draw only thin section lines, plus section column numbers along the top edge and row letters along the left edge (map-grid style), and drop the per-cell labels. Otherwise use outline-only labels. For ≤ 50 sections, also draw the sheet subdivision in thin grey with sheet numbers. For very large grids, add regional overview pages (e.g. 6×6 sections per page) instead of shrinking further.
corrected:
In src/core/pdf.ts, overview block (lines 265-296):

1. Work out `secMin`, the smallest section side on paper in mm. Take it from the median section size, not the minimum, so one narrow leftover edge section does not shrink every label. Set `fontPt = clamp(secMin/1.2, 5, 14)` and `boxH = fontPt*0.3528*1.35`. Replace the fixed `cy - 2.5, ..., 5` with `cy - boxH/2, ..., boxH`.

2. If `secMin < ~10 mm`, or a label box would be wider than about 70% of a section or taller than about 50% of it, switch to map-grid mode:
   - Leave about 5 mm of space to the left of and above the image (lower `x0` and `y0` by that amount and recompute `s`).
   - Draw only thin section lines (0.2 mm, orange).
   - Along the top edge, write the section column numbers (1..scols) at each column centre.
   - Along the left edge, write the section row letters (A..). Use the same row-letter function that builds `sec.id`, so the letter-plus-number IDs match exactly.
   - Add one short caption line, such as "Abschnitt = Zeilenbuchstabe + Spaltennummer, z. B. C7". It needs a new i18n key in de, en and tr.
   - Draw no per-section label boxes.

3. Otherwise keep the per-section labels, but make them see-through so the image shows: use a semi-transparent fill via jsPDF `GState({opacity:0.75})`, or white text with a thin dark outline and no fill.

4. Optional, lower priority: for very large grids (more than about 20 x 20 sections), add regional overview pages, each covering about 6 x 6 sections with full labels and the image crop behind them. Sheet boundaries are already shown on each section's cover page (pdf.ts:497-517), so they do not need to be added to the overall overview.

5. Add a vitest check that, for a 10000 x 5000 mm project with 300 mm sections on A4, no label is drawn larger than its section cell. For example, check in a test hook that the computed label box is smaller than the section size on paper, or that map-grid mode was chosen.

globalRules:
Implementation plan for making MosaicPlan "much, much better": 7 waves, 33 work packages, ordered by user impact. The order is: (1) data safety and geometric correctness; (2) workspace safety UI, Android platform, honest colours, honest preview, photo intake and design system; (3) mosaic colour quality, live preview, freeform editor, face/detail guidance, viewer features, PDF foundations and project portability; (4) cut placement and accent colours, laying workbench, progress engine, PDF sheet structure, offline face detector; (5) undo/redo, single-pass stats, viewer back-buffer, PDF content, shopping view, target colours, PDF export UI; (6) deviation map and batch editing, fine-tile materials, colour measuring, streaming CSV, final PDF wiring; (7) docs and e2e consolidation.

RULES FOR EVERY PACKAGE

Files and parallel work
- Packages in the same wave run in parallel. They own disjoint existing files.
- New files may be created freely, but each name must be unique to its package.
- Some packages add optional fields or parameters only so that a package in the next wave can compile. Each one is marked "contract for wave N". Add them exactly as written, even if nothing in your package uses them.

Translations (i18n)
- Put new keys in src/i18n/ext/<package-id>.ts and export {de, en, tr}. The aggregator in src/i18n/index.ts merges every ext file after the base dictionaries.
- All three languages must have the same keys and the same placeholders. tests/i18n.test.ts checks this.
- To change the wording of an existing key, override it in your own ext file. First grep src/i18n/ext to make sure no other ext file already overrides that key.
- Never edit de.ts, en.ts or tr.ts.

CSS
- Only w2-design-system edits src/ui/styles.css.
- Every other package puts its CSS in src/ui/css/<package-id>.css and imports it from a component it owns.

Tests
- Unit tests go in tests/<package-id>*.test.ts.
- Browser checks are standalone Playwright scripts at e2e/<package-id>.e2e.cjs, run against `npm run preview`.
- Only w7-docs-e2e touches e2e/run-e2e.cjs and README.md.
- The golden mosaic hash fixture is tests/golden/mosaic-hashes.json. It hashes kind, c1, c2, rec, sub, line, free and palette hex+code, but not names. It is owned by whichever package owns src/core/mosaic.ts in that wave. Any change to it must be deliberate and explained in the PR.

Quality bar
- Every package must leave `npm run typecheck`, `npm test`, `npm run build` and the existing `node e2e/run-e2e.cjs` green.
- Every package must keep the exact-geometry and count guarantees: totals equal the geometry, and cut dimensions come only from analyzeCut on real polygons.
- Anything estimated must be labelled 'Schätzung' or 'Richtwert'. Requirement 18 holds everywhere.
deferred: Grout compensation in computeMosaic (algo-quality#0, part 4). Both reviewers called it optional and off by default, and recommending a grout plus an honest preview gives most of the benefit. Changing the factory grout default from #BDB8AE to #808080 is deferred too; the recommendation never overwrites the user's choice.

Linear-light averaging of stone target colours (algo-quality#10). Measured gains are within k-means noise on natural photos. Revisit it together with linear-light resizing in imageOps, with a measured A/B benchmark.

Mixed tile sizes stage 2: zones with their own grid (spec-gaps#2). Wave 6 delivers stage 1, real fine-tile materials for k×k sub-stones plus fine regions. Zones touch every per-cell structure (progress mask, IDs, sections, hit-testing, PDF), and the tiles-step badge stays honest until then.

Movable section boundaries and a seam optimiser (spec-gaps#9). This is impact 2-3 and needs new settings across layout, viewer, worker and PDF. Paper-matched section presets (wave 6) cover the main paper-waste pain.
Full SVG export of plans and templates (spec-gaps#12). The vector PDF at 1:1 or custom paper already covers plotters. Only PNG preview export is built (wave 6).

Diff-based incremental statistics in a worker that keeps its own mosaic copy, and dirty-pixel overview updates (performance-scale#5, parts 2-3). They are replaced by the 8-13x single-pass stats (wave 5), coalesced stats jobs and O(1) progress counters (wave 4). Revisit only if 5M-stone edits are still slower than about 1 s.
Splitting the shape analysis across several workers (performance-scale#7, part b). The hot-loop fix gives about 4x. SharedArrayBuffer is not available without COOP/COEP headers.
One CSV per section, delivered as a ZIP (performance-scale#1). Streaming CSV plus the Excel row-limit warning are built; a store-only ZIP can follow if users ask.
Automatic stock-constrained recolouring (spec-gaps#4, part 4). It would change how the image looks and is often impossible. Exact shortfall and shopping lists are built instead.

Error-driven k-means swap refinement and detail-weighted palette samples (algo-quality#6, optional part). Measured gains were inconsistent. Pinned accent colours confirmed by the user are built instead.
Dither error diffusion through split/SUB cells, serpentine scanning and face/edge damping (algo-quality#1). Measured as useless or harmful.
Global cut budget, 'max. Schnittzellen' (algo-quality#3, phase 2). The background cut factor in wave 4 gives most of the value.
Image-level Canny/polyline contour extraction (algo-quality#5). Unproven, and it would defeat template reuse. Only the opt-in grid-preserving continuity bonus is built.
Haptic feedback with the VIBRATE permission (ux-mobile-android#2). The text status line and flash highlight already give feedback.
A native 'pause' flush registry through @capacitor/app (ux-mobile-android#1). beforeunload with commit(), visibilitychange and minimizeApp already cover saving.
MediaPipe face detection. Its 14.6 MB wasm exceeds the PWA precache limit; pico.js is used instead (wave 4).
Colour-chart sheet mode for measuring many tiles from one photo (spec-gaps#7, phase 2).
First-fit-decreasing packing of mixed-width strips into shared raw tiles (correctness-core#5, optional). The current per-shape-group count is a safe upper bound.
Mixed page orientations per section and tighter print margins (pdf-print#4). Mixed orientations risk print-dialog auto-scaling, which breaks 1:1. Smaller margins clip on common printers.
Undo history that persists across reloads (ux-desktop#7). The journal is in memory for the session only, and the README will say so.
